steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Use a fork to pierce the potato skins.
Bake the potatoes unwrapped for about 1 hour, or until soft, in the preheated oven.
Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.
Over medium-low heat melt the butter in a large saucepan. Combine onion, mushrooms, red pepper, garlic powder, pepper, chives and salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally until the onions are soft.

Slice open the baked potatoes and, keeping the skins intact, scoop the insides into a medium bowl. Transfer the onion mixture to the bowl. Mix in the sour cream. Pour in 1/2 of the cheese and continue mixing until all ingredients are well blended.
Using a large spoon, fill the potato skins with the mixture. Top with bread crumbs, the remaining cheese and bacon.
Return the potatoes to the preheated oven and continue baking for about 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the filling is slightly brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Twice Baked Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This is great as a side dish or as an appetizer. Melted cheese and crumbled bacon are the highlights of the flavorful, creamy filling.

review.reviewBody: Very good! I do recommend to cut back on the onion! I LOVE onions and I had doubled the recipe to make 8 potato's and halfed the onion's because it seemed like a lot to me and it was still very potent. Very good though! Thanks for the recipe! I will make this again!

I adjusted the recipe for making 10. When I got 2 1/2 onions chopped, I decided that it was twice as many onion as I wanted so I did not use at least half. Otherwise, it went well. We used a paring knife to loosen the potato from the skin and scooped it out with a spoon. This sped up that portion of the process nicely. Enjoy!

I made this for our Christmas dinner this year. My family likes spicy and these were pretty good but not as explosive as I imagined them (and talked them up) to be after reading prior reviews. I made some changes - I didn't have baking potatoes, so I used Yukon Golds and rather than re-stuffing them into the shells, since they're softer and not as "reliable" containers, I lined a casserole dish with the discarded skin pieces and layered the mixture on top. I added a few ingredients to mirror how I would build a "custom baked potato" based on what I had around the kitchen, and refrigerated the "once baked" casserole to re-bake the next day, making prep for a big family dinner much easier. The casserole was delicious and the leftovers were quickly eaten up. I will make this again!

Excellent! Depending in the size of the potatoes, bakers are pretty big (!), I'd personally make more of the mushroom and onion mix! I also added corned beef seasoned with garlic powder, salt and pepper, fried up, to the bottom of the potatoes covered with a bit of cheese. The left over corned beef, I mixed up into the potato mixture! Definitely a hit!

My husband and I LOVED it! I am glad that I made enough for left overs. The potatoes had lots of flavor! I like mushrooms, and he likes black olives so I added both. I omitted the red pepper, pepper, and chives (didn't have). I also left the bread crumbs out. The skins were so over stuffed that there wasn't room. I did top with the cheese and bacon. Also I used my mixer to cream the ingredients together. This recipe is well worth the effort. I will definitely make this again.

This had great depth of flavor. I didnt have sour cream so I subbed in milk then put the whole mix in the food processor. It turned out cream and delicious. Word of warning- I halved the cayenne and it still had a little kick.

This recipe is incredible - best twice-baked potatoes my family's ever had! I omitted the red peppers (based on other reviewers' comments that they made the potatoes too spicy for children) and the mushrooms (my husband doesn't care for them), and still, this side dish stole the show.

Because so many ingredients are added to the potato, I had lots of leftover "insides," so I made a cassarole with the leftovers by putting it in a cassarole dish, sprinkling it with breadcrumbs, extra cheese, and extra bacon. It was absolutely delicious!

This time, I used reduced-fat sour cream and cheese, and half regular bacon and half turkey bacon; next time, to make it healthier, I'll use fat free sour cream and cheese, and all turkey bacon.

Made a few changes but otherwise this is DELISH. Cut way down on the red pepper and a little less onion. I didn't use bread crumbs either. Next time I will cream the potatoes with the other ingredients to make it a little smoother and perhaps sale the potato skins and maybe pre-bake them a bit to make them crunchy. This is FANTASTIC.
Amazing with the kick of red pepper flakes! bread crumbs could be left out though. I made a bunch and froze then before the second bake. can't wait to have them more often. a big hit!
Very good, I skipped the onions and added seasoned shrimp!! BOMB

Fantastic recipe. Made it twice already and it comes out wonderful. I used very large baked potatoes so one potato serves 2. Had some leftovers so I froze 2 halves. After reheating they tasted pretty close to the experience of freshly made. The entire family agreed that this recipe is a keeper.
It was delicious! My family loved it!

This is one of our lakehouse favorites and is always a crowd pleaser. I make it following the recipe exactly but did omit the pepper flakes after my first couple because it was too hot for me. Awesome recipe and one of the rare ones that you just follow the recipe exactly to get 5 stars!!
Turned out great. Being a fan of flavorful food I added a dash of cumin.
These were awesome. Followed recipe since I had never made twice baked potatoes before - it was pretty perfect. Very rich. only needed one "half" per person and they were good as leftovers too!
My family absolutely loves these twice bakes. My daughter says there are the best she has ever had. One point is that I use about 1/2 the black and red pepper.
I added a tad more butter. Absolutely delicious recipe!
YUMMY! will definitely make it to!
